source.author: stat
source.text: At trepidus monstro et variis terroribus impar longaevi rex vatis opem tenebrasque sagaces Tiresiae, qui mos incerta paventibus, aeger consulit, ille deos non larga caede iuvencum, non alacri pinna aut verum salientibus extis, nec tripode implicito numerisque sequentibus astra, turea nec supra volitante altaria fumo tam penitus, durae quam Mortis limite manes elicitos patuisse refert, Lethaeaque sacra et mersum Ismeni subter confinia ponto miscentis parat ante ducem, circumque bidentum visceribus laceris et odori sulpuris aura graminibusque novis et longo murmure purgat.
source.text_original: At trepidus monstro et variis terroribus impar / longaevi rex vatis opem tenebrasque sagaces / Tiresiae, qui mos incerta paventibus, aeger / consulit, ille deos non larga caede iuvencum, / non alacri pinna aut verum salientibus extis, / nec tripode implicito numerisque sequentibus astra, / turea nec supra volitante altaria fumo / tam penitus, durae quam Mortis limite manes / elicitos patuisse refert, Lethaeaque sacra / et mersum Ismeni subter confinia ponto / miscentis parat ante ducem, circumque bidentum / visceribus laceris et odori sulpuris aura / graminibusque novis et longo murmure purgat.
source.text_english: But the king, terrified by the marvel and unequal to his many fears, sick at heart consults the aid and dark sagacity of Tiresias, the aged seer, who is the custom for the distraught to seek. He reports that the gods have not so fully disclosed the shades drawn forth within the boundary of hard Death, neither by lavish slaughter of calves, nor by the eager wing, nor by true entrails leaping, nor by the tripod entangled and the stars following in number, nor by incense smoke drifting above the altars, as he prepares the Lethaean rites before the leader, and mingles with them Ismenus, sunk beneath the confines of the sea that unites with it; and he purifies the place all around with the mangled entrails of goats, with the odor of sulfur, with fresh herbs, and with long-drawn murmur.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_original: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis / ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, / ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus / immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras / surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_english: As the fire, struggling amid the crowded entrails, brought forth the hair and climbed over the quivering innards of the bull, behold, the sacred Mopsus, wholly possessed by the god, terrible to see, was moving along the shore, his fillet and hair rising through the air, and he was brandishing laurel branches.
